c.v: A delivery robot quotes a job: a distance in metres and a waiting time in seconds. Three pricing rules can apply, a flat fee, a fee per kilometre and a fee per minute of waiting, and which one applies is decided when the quoting object is built. From memory, sketch the Strategy: write the point of variation as one operation, hold it in a

is the choice that fits this shape: the strategy is exactly one operation, the rule has to be chosen at run time from a tariff, and a
stays copyable. A base class would work too and costs a heap object per rule; a template parameter would be wrong here, because the tariff is read at run time.
You pass if the rule is a member the caller supplies, the quoting code names no rule, and you can say what the other two ways would have cost. Writing three
subclasses is a fail: that puts the variation in the class hierarchy, which is the thing Strategy exists to avoid.

Strategy is a pattern that isolates one step of an algorithm, the operation that varies, behind a name the rest of the algorithm calls without knowing which version runs. It differs from Command, which isolates a piece of work handed to something else once: a Strategy is a property of an object, chosen when the object is built and used on every call after.

The problem it solves is a step that would otherwise scatter across a family of near-identical classes. Three pricing rules that differ only in how they price a job could be written as three subclasses of the quoting object, but that puts the one thing that varies into the class hierarchy, so choosing a rule means choosing a class instead of passing a value.
The mechanism is holding that one operation as a value the object carries rather than as behaviour fixed in its class. Behind a small interface through a
, it is chosen and swapped at run time and open to any class that derives from the interface, for the pointer plus a heap object. As a

, it is equally swappable and accepts any matching callable, a lambda included, for a larger fixed size, but it can carry only that one operation. As a template parameter, it costs nothing at run time and the compiler can inline the call, but the choice is fixed when the program is built, which only fits when the caller decides, not a value read while running.
What it costs beyond the bytes is the call itself: one the compiler cannot see through, through a virtual function or a

, measured several times slower than an inlined call in a tight loop, though the gap disappears once the call does real work rather than sit in a microbenchmark. The pattern is also the wrong choice for a small, closed set of behaviours, which an enumeration and a switch check more directly, and for a step that never changes, which needs no variation to isolate.

Finally, the reason Strategy exists rather than subclassing the algorithm. Putting the variation in a

looks smaller today, and it multiplies: with three profiles and two logging modes it is six classes, and the next axis makes it twelve. A Strategy held as a member is one class and three settings structs, and the next axis is a second member.
